name: Digital Object Identifier
summary: Persistent alphanumeric identifier for a digital object. Use the resolvable form https://doi.org/{doi}.
notes: Default object identifier in the Blueprint. If a repository cannot mint DOIs, researchers can register with Crossref or DataCite.

name: Research Resource Identification
summary: Persistent identifier for key biological resources so they can be cited in papers.
notes: Often used for repositories, antibodies, cell lines, and software resources.

name: Uniform Resource Locator
summary: Common web locator. Globally unique and resolvable, but persistence depends on the host remaining committed.
notes: Listed as an alternative identifier. Weaker persistence than a resolvable DOI unless the organization guarantees it.

name: Internationalized Resource Identifier
summary: URL-like identifier that can include a wider character set than ASCII URLs.
notes: Table 2 lists IRI as a flexible identifier type. Many ontology terms are published as IRIs.

name: Open Researcher and Contributor Identifier
summary: Persistent identifier for researchers and other contributors.
notes: Default representation for the author field.

name: Research Organization Registry
summary: Identifier for research organizations such as universities, centers, and funders.
notes: Default for funder. Also listed as an author identifier when the creator is an organization.

name: International Standard Name Identifier
summary: Identifier for public identities of people and organizations that contribute to creative works.

name: NCBI Organismal Classification
summary: Ontology of organisms used for infectious agents and hosts.

name: MONDO Disease Ontology
summary: Disease and condition ontology used for healthCondition.
notes: Default for healthCondition. Other community ontologies may be acceptable when they interoperate.

name: NCI Thesaurus
summary: NCI Thesaurus terms for measurement techniques and related concepts.

name: SPDX License Identifier
summary: Short identifier for a standard software or data license.
notes: If the license is not in SPDX, use an IRI to the license document.
